summary: Three refrigerated containers exceeded the product temperature limit (E1) during a transfer in which relative humidity stayed above 88% for 73 minutes (E5). The evidence supports a two-factor interaction rather than a single cause: humidity-gated sensor calibration drift (E2) and the firmware retry defect that ignored every second restart command after a communications timeout (E3) were each insufficient alone. Containers carrying the firmware defect with calibrated sensors stayed within limit (E6), and containers carrying the drift with corrected restart logic also stayed within limit (E7), so each factor is necessary only in the presence of the other under the observed humidity condition. The 45-minute alert suppression (E4) is not part of the onset mechanism: it acted after the limit had already been crossed and extended operator response (E8), affecting exposure duration rather than whether the breach occurred. The principal unresolved point is the pathway by which an upward-reading drift produces an over-limit outcome, which the package does not state and which an independent reference probe would discriminate.

claims.statement: Three refrigerated containers exceeded the product temperature limit during a six-hour transfer.
Temperature sensor calibration drifted upward by about 1.5 C, and did so only while relative humidity exceeded 88%.
Relative humidity exceeded the 88% drift threshold for 73 minutes during the transfer, so the drift condition was active for part of the run.
A firmware retry defect caused the compressor controller to ignore every second restart command following a communications timeout.
The alerting rule suppressed repeated temperature alerts for 45 minutes after the first acknowledgement, and the delayed alert extended operator response after the limit had already been crossed.
In a comparison run, containers with the same firmware defect but calibrated sensors did not exceed the product limit.
In a comparison run, containers with the same sensor drift but corrected restart logic did not exceed the product limit.
The breach required the joint presence of humidity-gated sensor drift and the firmware retry defect; neither factor alone was sufficient under otherwise comparable conditions.
The humidity excursion above 88% was the enabling condition that activated the drift arm of the interaction; without it the drift factor would not have been present during the transfer.

Alert suppression did not contribute to the onset of the breach and acted only on post-crossing exposure duration, because its effect on operator response occurred after the limit was already exceeded.

relationships.rationale: The drift is reported as occurring only above 88% RH, and humidity crossed that threshold during the transfer, so the humidity excursion is the condition under which the drift became active.
The humidity excursion supplies the drift arm of the interaction; it acts on the outcome only through the drift, not directly.
Sensor drift is one of the two factors present in the breaching containers, but the comparison run shows it is not sufficient on its own.
The restart defect is the second factor present in the breaching containers, and the comparison run shows it is likewise not sufficient on its own.
Firmware defect with calibrated sensors staying within limit rules out the defect as a sufficient single cause.
Sensor drift with corrected restart logic staying within limit rules out the drift as a sufficient single cause.
Removing the drift arm by calibrating sensors broke the conjunction and the outcome did not occur despite the defect remaining.
Removing the defect arm by correcting restart logic broke the conjunction and the outcome did not occur despite the drift remaining.
The evidence places the extended operator response after the temperature had already crossed the product limit.
Suppression and the delayed response are located downstream of the crossing, which is the basis for treating them as exposure-duration effects rather than onset causes.

The defect is conditioned on a communications timeout, but the package does not record whether or how often timeouts occurred in the affected containers, so the activation of this arm is asserted only by the comparison-run contrast.

An upward-reading drift would be expected to bias a controller toward more cooling, and the package does not state the pathway by which it instead contributes to an over-limit outcome or how much of the recorded exceedance is measurement artifact.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the recorded exceedance reflects actual product temperature or is partly an artifact of the upward 1.5 C drift, and by what pathway an upward-reading sensor contributes to a real over-limit condition.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: An independent, humidity-insensitive reference probe or product-side temperature log from the three affected containers, compared against the drifted sensor trace over the same interval.

uncertainties.statement: Whether communications timeouts, the precondition for the firmware defect, actually occurred in the affected containers and whether the humidity excursion or transfer conditions induced them.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Controller timeout and restart-command event logs for the three containers, time-aligned with the relative humidity trace.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the two comparison runs were comparable to the failing transfer in ambient load, duration, door openings, and humidity exposure, which the package does not state.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Run metadata for both comparison runs showing duration and time above 88% RH alongside the same figures for the failing transfer.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the three breaching containers shared any further common attribute beyond drift and defect, such as unit model, age, or position in the load.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Per-container configuration and load-position inventory for the breaching and non-breaching containers on the same transfer.

uncertainties.statement: Whether a 1.5 C bias plus missed alternate restarts is quantitatively sufficient to account for the observed exceedance margin.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Recorded peak temperature and time-over-limit against the product limit, with compressor duty-cycle data for the same window.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the 45-minute suppression window materially changed product outcome, given that it began only after acknowledgement of an alert raised post-crossing.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Timestamps of limit crossing, first alert, first acknowledgement, and corrective action, compared with the product's cumulative time-over-limit tolerance.

actions.action: Correct the firmware retry logic so that no restart command is ignored after a communications timeout.
actions.mechanismTargeted: Removes the restart-failure arm of the two-factor conjunction (C4).
actions.rationale: E7 shows directly that containers with corrected restart logic stayed within the product limit even while carrying the sensor drift. Breaking either arm is sufficient, and this arm is deterministic and independent of ambient conditions, so the fix does not depend on humidity exposure remaining within any assumed range.

actions.action: Recalibrate the temperature sensors and adopt humidity-compensated or humidity-insensitive sensing above 88% RH.
actions.mechanismTargeted: Removes the drift arm of the conjunction (C2, C9).
actions.rationale: E6 shows calibrated sensors prevented the breach despite the defect being present. Deploying this alongside A1 gives defense in depth on both arms, and it also improves telemetry fidelity, which bears on U1. It ranks below A1 only because its effectiveness is tied to environmental conditions rather than being unconditional.

actions.action: Revise the alerting rule so that suppression does not apply to an ongoing or worsening excursion, only to repeat notifications within a stable band.
actions.mechanismTargeted: Shortens post-crossing exposure duration via operator response time (C5, C10).
actions.rationale: E8 places this effect strictly after the limit crossing, so it cannot prevent onset. It is worth doing to limit exposure and product loss, but it should not displace A1 or A2 as a preventive measure.

actions.action: Instrument and alert on relative humidity crossing the 88% threshold during transfers.
actions.mechanismTargeted: Surfaces the enabling condition for the drift arm (C3, C9).
actions.rationale: Monitoring alone does not break either arm of the conjunction, so it is not preventive by itself; its value is giving early warning that a container has entered the regime in which the drift becomes active, and supplying data for U3.

actions.action: Fit an independent reference temperature probe on a sample of containers.
actions.mechanismTargeted: Diagnostic only; does not act on either causal arm.
actions.rationale: Resolves U1 by separating real product temperature from drifted sensor readings. If the exceedance proves to be partly artifact, the relative priority of A1 and A2 would change, so this is worth running in parallel rather than after the fixes.

counterfactuals.change: A container carrying both the sensor drift and the firmware defect, with humidity above 88%, stayed within the product limit.
counterfactuals.implication: The conjunction would not be sufficient, indicating a further necessary factor present in the three breaching containers but absent here.

counterfactuals.change: A container with both calibrated sensors and corrected restart logic nonetheless exceeded the limit on the same transfer.
counterfactuals.implication: An unmeasured common cause would be implicated, and both A1 and A2 would be insufficient as remedies.

counterfactuals.change: Logs show no communications timeout occurred in the three breaching containers.
counterfactuals.implication: The firmware defect could not have been active, defeating the interaction account and reopening a single-factor drift explanation that E7 would then contradict, forcing re-examination of comparison-run comparability.

counterfactuals.change: An independent reference probe shows product temperature never actually exceeded the limit.
counterfactuals.implication: The outcome would be a measurement artifact of the drift, making A2 and telemetry integrity the priority and reducing A1 to an unrelated latent defect.

counterfactuals.change: Breaches occurred among drift-and-defect containers during an interval when humidity never exceeded 88%.
counterfactuals.implication: The drift would not be humidity-gated as E2 states, or a different arm is operative, undermining humidity as the enabling condition and weakening A4.

counterfactuals.change: Timestamps show the first alert acknowledgement preceded the limit crossing, so suppression was already in force as the temperature rose.
counterfactuals.implication: Alert suppression would move from a downstream exposure effect into the onset pathway, raising A3 above A4 and possibly above A2 in priority.
